messages.text:
"Make a creature tower defense game. You play as a trainer defending your base from waves of wild creatures.

How it works:
- A map with a winding path. Enemies walk along it toward my base.
- I place my own cute original creatures on the empty tiles to attack them.
- Creatures have types (Fire, Water, Grass, Electric, Rock, Wind) with strengths and weaknesses. Example: Water beats Fire, Fire beats Grass, Grass beats Water.
- Each creature has a special ability: slow, area damage, poison, or stun.
- Creatures evolve into stronger forms when upgraded (3 stages).

Gameplay:
- I earn energy by defeating enemies and spend it to place or upgrade creatures.
- 30 waves, with a boss every 10 waves.
- Enemy types: fast, tanky, flying, and boss.
- My base has 20 HP. I lose at 0 HP and win after wave 30.
- After each wave, I choose 1 new creature out of 3 to add to my team.

Controls and look:
- Touch controls: tap to place, tap a creature to upgrade or sell.
- Buttons for pause, 2x speed, and start next wave.
- Colorful pixel art style, with attack effects, health bars, and floating damage numbers.
- Top bar shows base HP, energy, and wave number.

Start with 1 map, 6 creatures, and 10 waves. Keep it simple and fun.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable creature tower defense game in the existing project.

## Requirements
- Winding-path map, placeable original creatures, six elemental types with strengths/weaknesses, abilities, and three evolution stages.
- Earn and spend energy, defend a 20-HP base, face enemy varieties and bosses, choose a creature after each wave, and provide touch-friendly placement, pause, speed, and wave controls.
- Colorful pixel-art-inspired visuals with attack effects, health bars, damage numbers, and a top HUD.
- User asked to start with one map, six creatures, and 10 waves; the request also mentions 30 waves, so the assistant implemented 10 waves.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Implemented a standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with canvas-drawn map and creatures, no framework or external game dependencies.
- Used original creature names and emoji-based visuals; wave 10 is the boss wave.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js` with the game UI and core mechanics.
- Added six creature types, wave progression, enemy types, combat and abilities, upgrades/selling, post-wave choices, and win/loss states.
- `node --check game.js` passed.

### Active
- Browser verification and any resulting fixes remain to be done.

### Blocked
- `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` failed because the Playwright-managed Chromium is missing: `Browser "chromium" is not installed; expected executable at /home/runner/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1243/chrome-linux64/chrome.`

## Next Move
1. Install the Playwright browser with `playwright-cli install-browser chromium`, then open `http://localhost:3002` and verify the rendered game and basic interactions.
2. Fix any issues found and save/read the latest small JPEG screenshot as requested.
3. Finish with a concise summary including the 10-wave assumption.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game page structure and HUD, controls, dialogs.
- `style.css`: Responsive layout and visual styling.
- `game.js`: Game state, mechanics, canvas rendering, and event handlers.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; new project files currently show as untracked.
- A local server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- The browser verification attempt has not yet produced a screenshot.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable creature tower defense game in the existing project.

## Requirements
- Winding-path map, placeable original creatures, six elemental types with strengths and weaknesses, special abilities, and three evolution stages.
- Earn and spend energy, defend a 20-HP base, face varied enemies and bosses, choose a creature after each wave, and provide touch-friendly placement, pause, speed, and wave controls.
- Colorful pixel-art-inspired visuals with attack effects, health bars, damage numbers, and a top HUD.
- Start with one map, six creatures, and 10 waves; wave 10 is the boss wave.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them when finished.
- Save small JPEG screenshots (viewport at most 1280px wide) and inspect only the latest.

## Decisions
- Built a standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with canvas-drawn map and creatures, no framework or external game dependencies.
- Used original creature names and emoji-based visuals.
- When all six creatures are unlocked, post-wave choices provide a team damage boost and energy instead of a duplicate recruit.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js` implementing the interface, map, creatures, combat, abilities, upgrades/selling, wave choices, and win/loss states.
- Installed Playwright Chromium and opened the game at `http://localhost:3002`.
- Captured and inspected `screenshots/wildbound-latest.jpg`; the initial game screen rendered successfully.
- `node --check game.js` passed.

### Active
- Browser-playtest placement and wave progression; investigate the single browser console 404 for `/favicon.ico` if useful.
- Fix any gameplay or rendering issues found, then refresh and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run browser interactions to place creatures, start a wave, and confirm combat, HUD, and wave transitions.
2. Fix any issues found and save/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.
3. Finish with a concise summary, including the 10-wave assumption.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game page structure, HUD, controls, dialogs.
- `style.css`: Responsive layout and visual styling.
- `game.js`: Game state, mechanics, canvas rendering, and event handlers.
- `screenshots/wildbound-latest.jpg`: Latest inspected initial-state screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- A local server is running at `http://localhost:3002`.
- The initial browser load showed one console error: 404 for `/favicon.ico`.

Implemented **Wildbound — Creature Keepers** as a playable, standalone tower defense game.

- Added a winding trail, six original elemental creatures, combat abilities, upgrades through three evolution stages, varied enemies, and a boss on wave 10.
- Added energy and base-HP systems, wave rewards, pause and speed controls, and touch-friendly placement.
- Fixed the missing favicon request.
- Playtested placement, combat, wave completion, recruit choices, and the next wave. `node --check game.js` passes.
- Saved and inspected the latest viewport screenshot at `screenshots/wildbound-latest.jpg` (1050 × 793).

Assumption: the game has one map and 10 waves; when all creatures are recruited, wave rewards offer team upgrades and energy instead of duplicate recruits.
